To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unidimensional IRT models provide valid interpretation of test scores when administering tests with items that are sensitive to multiple latent traits.

unidimensional IRT models are generally robust to the presence of secondary dimensions from sensitive item(s) and that longer tests are more resistant to the violation of unidimensionality than shorter ones.
unidimensional IRT models provide valid interpretation of test scores even when items sensitive to secondary dimensions are administered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity of inferences made from the application of univariate item response models to test results from tests that include items with secondary dimensions.
whether the application of IRT models to tests with secondary dimensions provides valid interpretation of the test results.

the robustness of unidimensional models to the violation of unidimensionality due to sensitive items and the effect of the violation of unim dimensionality on the accuracy of ability measurement and the estimation of item parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

unidimensional IRT models are generally robust to the violation due to secondary dimensions, although the degree of robustness depends on the degree of secondary dimensionality and the length of test.
unidimensional model can be applied to tests with items sensitive to secondary dimensions with some caution.
the violation of the strict unidimensionality due to secondary dimensions has little influence on the accuracy of ability estimates and the validity of test results in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the secondary dimensions are highly related to the main construct, it is not necessary to remove the secondary dimensions from tests.
unidimensional IRT models can provide valid interpretation of test scores even in the presence of secondary dimensions.
unidimensional IRT models can be used in practice when there is a concern that some items may be sensitive to secondary dimensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of univariate item response models to tests with items sensitive to secondary dimensions is generally acceptable and the use of such models is not necessarily problematic.
unidimensional IRT models can be used in many situations to estimate ability, even when items are sensitive to more than one dimension.
unidimensional tests with items sensitive to secondary dimensions may be used to make inferences about the main construct.
